Overview We introduce Video Prediction Policy 2 (VPP2) , a world-action model (WAM) with strong zero-shot generalization in both video prediction and action generation. Our pipeline has three stages: (1) event-level video pretraining , (2) single-step visual planning through post-training and distillation , and (3) action learning with a mixture-of-transformers (MoT) architecture . This codebase includes: Zero-shot video prediction . Generate videos from an initial image and a text instruction using the Stage-1 (49 frames) or Stage-2 (17 frames) video model, with input preparation, prompt enhancement, and ready-to-run examples. Policy post-training on RoboDojo and LIBERO . Training configurations and scripts for adapting VPP2 to both benchmarks, together with policy evaluation workflows. For RoboDojo, we add history frames to the model input to support tasks that require memory. To accommodate this architecture change, we start post-training from the Stage-2 video model before distillation . live_web_research.page_text: Video Prediction Policy 2: Predict Better, Act Better | Arxiv - DeepPaper Video Prediction Policy 2: Predict Better, Act Better PDF DeepRead Key Contributions Introduced VPP2, a world action model that achieves superior zero-shot generalization in robotic manipulation by combining large-scale manipulation-specific pretraining, visual planning distillation, and a mixture-of-transformers action module. Abstract World action models (WAMs) have emerged as an important class of generalist robot policies, aiming to transfer video prediction priors to action learning. However, we find that existing WAMs frequently produce incorrect motion predictions in open-ended environment, leading to erroneous actions. We attribute this limitation to two factors: (1) base video models are not optimized for manipulation, and (2) naively incorporating action components into video models can substantially degrade their generalization capabilities. We introduce Video Prediction Policy 2 (VPP2), a WAM that enables strong zero-shot generalization in both video prediction and action generation. First, we curate a large-scale, diverse dataset of manipulation videos to continue pretraining the base video foundation model. We annotate video clips with detailed captions and perform \textit{event-level} video pretraining to promote generalization across open-ended manipulation tasks. Second, we post-train and distill the video model into a single-step visual planner with fixed prediction horizon. Finally, we introduce action module via a mixture-of-transformers (MoT) architecture to learn implicit inverse dynamics model. Experiments demonstrate three key results: (1) VPP2-14B outperforms Cosmos3-64B by 11.0\% points in video prediction instruction-following success rate on open-ended tasks; (2) VPP2 surpasses the strongest baseline by 18.5\% points in success rate on real-world zero-shot ALOHA manipulation tasks; and (3) following benchmark-specific post-training, VPP2 achieves the highest success rates among evaluated methods on the challenging LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-OOD, and RoboDojo benchmarks. Summary VPP2 is a novel world action model that improves robotic manipulation through specialized pretraining, visual planning distillation, and a mixture-of-transformers architecture for implicit inverse dynamics. article.body:
Robotera-linked team reports VPP2 robot-manipulation tests; deployment unestablished

Researchers including Robotera introduce Video Prediction Policy 2 (VPP2) in an arXiv paper, describing a model for video prediction and robot action generation. They report tests on real-world zero-shot ALOHA manipulation tasks and robotics benchmarks. The paper is a research report, not a government policy, contract or deployment; it does not establish operational use by a public body or service. The team’s reported test results therefore do not show that VPP2 is fielded or ready for routine use.
